elements.requirement: A person is guilty of an offence under section 3ZD of the Road Traffic Act 1988 if that person causes serious injury to another person by driving a motor vehicle on a road.
elements.quote: causes serious injury to another person by driving a motor vehicle on a road

elements.requirement: A person driving a motor vehicle is only guilty of the offence under section 3ZD of the Road Traffic Act 1988 if, at the time of causing serious injury, that person is committing an offence under section 103(1)(b) of the Act (driving while disqualified).
elements.quote: at that time, is committing an offence under section 103(1)(b) of this Act (driving while disqualified)

elements.requirement: In England and Wales, 'serious injury' for the purposes of section 3ZD of the Road Traffic Act 1988 means physical harm which amounts to grievous bodily harm for the purposes of the Offences against the Person Act 1861.
elements.quote: in England and Wales, physical harm which amounts to grievous bodily harm for the purposes of the Offences against the Person Act 1861

elements.requirement: In Scotland, 'serious injury' for the purposes of section 3ZD of the Road Traffic Act 1988 means severe physical injury.
